account_signal_summary: Harbor Analytics looks like a post-Series B sales scaling account: about 140 employees, $30M raised ten months ago, a new VP of Sales, 12 open sales roles, and no visible RevOps hire yet. The strongest GTM angle is helping Priya keep pipeline visibility, discovery quality, and manager coaching from getting messy as the team grows.

emails.subject: Scaling Harbor's sales team
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

Congrats on joining Harbor. I saw the team is hiring 12 sales roles after the Series B.

When a new VP inherits that kind of hiring plan before RevOps is fully built, pipeline visibility usually gets messy fast. Reps work hard, but managers cannot see which accounts are real, stale, or at risk.

We help sales leaders turn account signals, call notes, and CRM data into a cleaner weekly operating rhythm.

Worth comparing notes for 15 minutes?

Best,
Danny

emails.subject: Re: Scaling Harbor's sales team
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

One thought I should have included: the risk is not just reporting. It is coaching.

If Harbor adds AEs and SDRs quickly, your managers will need a consistent way to spot weak discovery, missing next steps, and deals that look active but have no real buyer movement.

That is the workflow we focus on: turn messy GTM signals into usable manager actions.

Open to a quick conversation next week?

Best,
Danny

emails.subject: Harbor + RevOps gap
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

Last note from me.

Harbor looks like it is in the exact moment where sales process matters: new VP, recent funding, fast hiring, no obvious RevOps owner yet.

If pipeline inspection or rep coaching becomes a priority as the team scales, I would be happy to share the account-review framework we use with growth-stage teams.

Best,
Danny

emails.subject: Close the loop?
emails.body:
Hi Priya,

I will close the loop after this.

If sales hiring is already covered, no need to reply. If pipeline visibility or discovery coaching starts to feel too manual as Harbor scales, I can send over a short worksheet for account reviews.

Either way, congrats again on the new role.

Best,
Danny
